declarations.historical_source: A. Rosa, On certain valuations of the vertices of a graph, Theory of Graphs (Rome, 1966), 1967, pp. 349-355
declarations.normalized_statement: Every finite tree with m edges has an injective vertex labeling into {0,...,m} whose absolute edge differences are exactly {1,...,m}.

declarations.source: A. Kotzig, cited in A. Rosa, On certain valuations of the vertices of a graph, 1967
declarations.normalized_statement: For every n-edge tree, cyclic shifts modulo 2n+1 of one embedding give 2n+1 pairwise edge-disjoint copies whose union is K_(2n+1).

declarations.source: G. Ringel, Problem 25, Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Smolenice, 1963), 1964
declarations.normalized_statement: For every n-edge tree, K_(2n+1) decomposes into 2n+1 pairwise edge-disjoint copies of the tree.
The Ringel and stronger cyclic Kotzig conclusions hold for every sufficiently large n.

transfer_cluster.kind: strict implication chain, not duplicate declarations and not a shared numerical residual wall
non_implications: A Kotzig/rho labeling need not place all tree vertices in {0,...,n}, so the literature does not identify Kotzig with graceful labeling.
Ringel decomposition forgets cyclic coherence and does not imply Kotzig.
transfer_cluster.literature_coordinate: Kotzig is equivalent to a rainbow tree in the near-distance coloring, or equivalently a rho-labeling; graceful labeling imposes the extra vertex-range restriction {0,...,n}.

status_gate.claim_audit: arXiv:2202.03178 claims a proof of the graceful tree conjecture, but current authoritative and 2025/2026 literature continues to classify the conjecture as open; the claim is not treated as an accepted resolution.

proved_domains: Every tree through 35 vertices is reported computationally graceful by W. Fang, arXiv:1003.3045v2.
Every path is graceful by the classical alternating-extremes labeling.
Every sufficiently large n satisfies the cyclic Kotzig conclusion, hence Ringel, by Montgomery-Pokrovskiy-Sudakov, arXiv:2001.02665 / GAFA 2021.

candidate_wall.seed: P3, the two-edge path with ordered vertices a-b-c
candidate_wall.equality: The induced difference set is exactly {1,2}; cyclic shifts give the exact K5 decomposition, which also satisfies Ringel.
candidate_wall.obstruction: The natural residual is Boolean/existential rather than signed. Subdividing an end edge of P3 preserves the path class, whose alternating-extremes graceful labeling is a theorem for every length.
candidate_wall.catalogue_transformation_considered: Replace end edge b-c by a path with t new degree-two vertices, for a prospective bounded grid t=1,...,12.
candidate_wall.directional_prediction: tree order and edge count increase by t; graceful/Kotzig/Ringel truth remains pinned true because every output is a path.

stop.reason: Every output of the only exact obstruction-derived catalogue transformation from the equality seed is a path, hence already graceful and therefore already Kotzig and Ringel. Evaluating the twelve positive instances cannot test a crossing or distinguish the implication levels.
stop.next_lane_requirement: A future contract must name a non-path seed and a transformation that leaves all established graceful classes and the sufficiently-large Kotzig/Ringel domain, while freezing a falsifiable failure certificate for the existential conclusion.
